b:
Drink ruins the home

Drinking is a curse on the country and the home

These are philosophical words Tamil cinema let fall. But the sad thing is that they have all stayed just words. Alcohol is a killer that has spread across the world, beyond any one culture. Though in this century there is a society that looks down on drinking, among the young, drinking is seen as an expression of manhood, or an act of bravery, or the height of fun. Especially among the educated, parties don't end without alcohol.

In many homes, alcohol is handed down by the older generation to the younger as a gift. It is breaking it, in the sense of "break the chain", that is hard. Something approved by your own family won't strike the next generation as wrong. Those who never feel that generational influence are gifted people.

Alcohol must have appeared along with the growth of human civilisation. A drink made of rice and honey from 7000 years before the common era has been found in China. That is the witness to the story of alcohol and humans growing up together. Likewise, jars of alcohol have been found in ancient civilisations such as Iran, Mesopotamia and Egypt.

Tamils were no slouches either. Sangam poems mention many kinds of toddy. History says even Grandmother Avvai drank toddy with Pari. (That she and the Avvai who gave us the moral verses were different people is another story.) The Vedas mention soma. Later, under the influence of Buddhism and Jainism, abstinence became popular. The Manusmriti called drinking by Brahmins a terrible sin. The Thirukkural, which came after the Sangam age, gave a whole chapter to praising abstinence from toddy. Valluvar called toddy poison. Ayurveda says the same.

Medicine came to see alcohol, steeped into Western culture, as an enemy only late in the day. Before that, it is unfortunate that it became the culture of the elite, and then the culture of Asians who follow in their footsteps. Even in Sri Lanka, where Buddhism, which rejected alcohol, flourished, alcohol keeps spreading its branches. What can the Buddha do. It is some comfort that many great minds, Pythagoras, Plato, Lincoln, Gandhi, rejected alcohol and set an example for many. In every age there is a need for some famous person to come and remind us of this.

Drinking apparently takes roughly 20,000 to 23,000 lives in Sri Lanka. That is 65 people a day. Whoever comes must one day go. But alcohol stands as the leading cause of death among those aged 25 to 45. Drinking is the cause of 60 percent of liver failure in Sri Lanka. Liver failure doesn't kill at once. Death finally comes only after going through many sufferings, with frequent trips to hospital for vomiting blood, a swollen belly and a confused mind. It is Sri Lanka's free health service that carries this burden. This society, which expects those who studied through free education to serve for free, doesn't think about this burden. Directly, 69 to 140 billion rupees a year. That is spent directly on things like intensive care. Beyond this, figures say there is a loss of nearly 199 to 266 billion rupees from lost manpower. In total, roughly 2 percent of gross domestic product a year, that is 335 billion rupees, is seen as the economic loss due to alcohol.

Beyond this, 19.3 percent of all road accidents are found to happen under the influence of drink. Films show drinking as the answer to stress. In reality it reduces the chemicals that relieve stress. It reduces the amount of sleep. Over time it increases suicidal thinking. The super songs of the silver screen don't show this. It is the sorrow of this land that a society that thumps its chest saying our forefather Tamils drank toddy forgets those who drank toddy and lost their minds.

Alcohol is a poison

Alcohol is not a celebration

Alcohol becomes death

Those who sleep are no different from the dead;
those who drink toddy are forever drinking poison.
note: Avvaiyar is the name of more than one Tamil poetess: the Sangam-age poet who was a friend of the chieftains, and the later author of the children's moral verses. The closing couplet is Thirukkural 926.
